question: X6: desktop rows of Summary, Pricing Plan, Newsletter, Instagram, Bandsintown and Scheduling, pulled in by the east handle one column at a time to the floor, then out to 24 columns, area and content height at each step; then a new one pulled far in from the west
answer: A side pull gives a block the rows its content needs at the new width, ceil((height + 11) / 41.1 - 0.02), and never gives rows back as it widens. Instagram is the exception: its rows follow its tiles both ways, with up to 0.13 of a row of give (over 0.106, under 0.16). A new Bandsintown starts at 5 rows over 815 of content and takes rows only when pulled. Timing: a one-column pull on Summary sets rows from its content before it reflows (13 columns kept 11 rows over 735), and the next pull catches up; Instagram's first pull and a far pull from the west land a step behind the same way. Summary's content moves between sessions: CAP-X6STEPS.json read 14 rows at 17 columns, this read 11. Not compared: Summary's pulls from 8 columns on moved nothing, its handle pressed but not taken; the first Summary stayed in the section and later reads hold it too.
ours: Ours holds these heights as a table by columns on desktop, measurements only, and a side pull takes their rows; Instagram's tiles already drew the oracle's heights to 0.1 px, and its rows now follow them both ways. npm run x6-check replays this read: 127 of 127, 4 named (the timing reads).
